description: Style anchor for Home Field hub art. Every imagegen prompt MUST include this description verbatim under a `Style anchor` block so terrain, props, exits, chibi, and effects read as one cohesive world.

style.world: Mycelium fungal forest meadow with a cute dark occult storybook mood: cozy, eerie, ritual-woodland, playful danger, organic and bioluminescent. Inspired by modern cute-goth roguelite hub worlds without copying any specific game, character, logo, symbol set, or composition.

palette.primary: deep moss green and muted fungal teal grass with chunky readable patches (#315f38, #456f3f, #244b35)
palette.accents: warm candle-amber bioluminescence (#d9902f, #f0bc54), muted violet ritual glow (#6e4aa5, #9d73c9), bone parchment neutrals (#e6dcc3), small blood-red/toadstool accents only as rare focal marks (#8f2f2a)
palette.shadows: soft warm umber and plum-brown shadows, never pure black (#2b201d, #332536)

style.lighting: Moody dusk with a warm candlelit top-left key and soft violet fill. High readability over realism. Simple graphic light shapes, gentle vignette feeling, no harsh sun, no realistic hard cast shadows.
style.outline: Bold clean storybook outline on props, exits, effects, and chibi: dark plum/umber linework, rounded and slightly irregular, close to black but warmer. Terrain usually has no hard outline; it uses broad flat color fields, soft edge transitions, and a few simple hand-drawn grass strokes.
style.shapeLanguage: Cute-goth storybook shapes: chunky silhouettes, squat mushrooms, carved organic arches, rounded-but-sinister curves, simplified graphic clusters, clear negative space, sticker-like readability at small size. Prefer simple iconic shapes over delicate high-detail painting.
style.texture: Flat-to-soft shaded 2D game art with cut-paper/storybook layering, minimal micro-detail, and visible hand-drawn strokes. Surfaces should feel graphic and intentionally simple, not photoreal, over-rendered, or noisy.
style.terrainReference: For the home field floor, target a simple top-down cartoon forest meadow like a modern cute-goth roguelite hub: broad muted green ground, low-detail moss shadows, a few dark grass strokes, occasional small yellow-green marks, and lots of open readable space. Bushes, flowers, mushrooms, vines, gates, and decorative objects belong on separate transparent object layers, not baked into repeatable terrain tiles.
style.productionBar: Production assets must look like hand-authored game art, not script-generated placeholders. Terrain should be simple and quiet, but with tasteful color harmony, organic asymmetry, and no visible seams or wallpaper rhythm. Props carry most of the visual personality through bold silhouettes, transparent alpha, dark storybook outlines, compact blob shadows, and consistent scale against the chibi.
style.sceneFit: The composed screen should read like a real in-game hub screenshot: chibi mushroom-elf characters standing on a soft green meadow, with chunky dark-ink foliage and props around them. Grass is the readable stage, not the star. Object-layer bushes, vines, mushrooms, exits, and flowers frame the scene and create charm without making the walkable center noisy.
style.chibiFit: Chibi avatars are small, squat, expressive mushroom-elf heroines with oversized heads, visible feet, simple readable costumes, warm dark outlines, and clear bottom grounding. Grass and props must leave enough visual rest around their feet so the characters do not disappear into texture.
style.shadowStyle: Soft compact blob shadows under ground entities using semi-transparent warm umber/plum. Shadows are graphic and readable, not long or physically realistic.
style.ambient: Sparse drifting spores, candle-amber motes, muted violet ritual glow, tiny fungal runes or abstract marks only when they are not readable text. Tone is cozy, eerie, magical, and playful — cute dark fairytale rather than horror.
style.scale: 2.5D top-down RPG hub camera, slightly elevated and orthographic-ish. Big readable objects, exaggerated proportions, mushrooms taller than the chibi, chibi feet clearly grounded.

rejections: No medieval stone, no sci-fi, no urban props
No bright cartoon colors, no neon, no rainbow palettes
No high-contrast pure-black outlines or pure-white highlights
No realistic photography or photoreal textures
No realistic grass-blade detail, no soft generic fantasy painting, no over-detailed concept-art rendering
No visible procedural/math pattern, repeated brush stamp, checkerboard-like distribution, or developer-placeholder geometry in production assets
No direct copying of Cult of the Lamb characters, icons, cult symbols, UI, logo shapes, or exact art compositions
No text in the images themselves — signposts are art-only; text is rendered at runtime
No human-only figures with mushroom hats; chibis are mushroom-elf heroines with visible elf ears when ears are shown
sources: docs/home-field-ingame-plan.md (Visual Concept and Visual And Scale Lock sections)
